subject: Private deployment: network & performance SLOs - post-call recap
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: network & performance SLOs - notes and next steps

Hi Kate,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the private/VPC performance qualification for FintechAI. High-level items we captured: 

- Acceptance targets (FintechAI ask): p95 end-to-end latency <= 200ms for request/response (streaming gestures allowed up to p95 300ms), sustained throughput 250 requests/sec with spikes to 600 rps for 5m, concurrency target of 120 concurrent streams.
- Model footprint: 4-shard LLM (12B equivalent), ~4GB per-worker KV cache during sustained sessions.
- Network expectations: private VPC peering preferred; fallback via VPN with route-based BGP. Egress firewall will only allow outbound to a small set of IPs (we'll provide).
- Observability/validation: NetOps will provide traceroutes, perf endpoints; FintechAI will run synthetic traffic and share packet captures for initial baseline.

What we need from your side to kick off the lab qualification: 
1) Temporary test VPC/Peering details OR VPN endpoint + CIDR to accept for Redwood test agents.
2) Firewall egress allowlist (IP/port) we can use for the lab.
3) Sample synthetic traffic profile (RPS curvature, request size, streaming vs non-streaming split).
4) Preferred window for a 90-minute lab test next week (we suggested Thu 03/18 10:00–11:30 PT).

I attached a starter SLO worksheet and a sample pcap we discussed. Rafael & Marissa are copied for technical alignment — Rafael will run initial kernel-level perf checks on Redwood side and Marissa will coordinate the lab.

Next steps: once we receive the VPN/peering details and the synthetic profile, Redwood will provision an isolated test harness in our private lab, run three ramp tests (baseline, sustained load, and burst), and produce an end-to-end report with latency histograms and recommendations (quantization or batching changes) within 48 hours of the test.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
pri y.om.das@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@fintechai.com>

Cc: netops@fintechai.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network & performance SLOs - notes and next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the acceptance targets are correct from our side. A few clarifications from NetOps: 

- We prefer VPC peering (Cross-account VPC peering within AWS). VPN is acceptable as a fallback for the initial lab.
- Firewall will allow outbound to 3rd-party IPs once we get a concrete list; can you provide the exact IPs/ports your test agents use?
- For synthetic profile: we typically do a 70/30 split non-streaming/streaming; median request payload ~1.2KB; streaming sessions hold an open connection and send incremental tokens for ~6–8 seconds.

We can make the lab window on Thu 03/18 10:00–11:30 PT. I will loop in our NetOps team to share traceroutes and a preliminary packet capture from our staging environment.

Kate Ellis
Head of Integrations
FintechAI
kate.ellis@fintechai.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@fintechai.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: network & performance SLOs - notes and next steps

On Tue, 10 Mar 2026 at 15:08, Kate Ellis <kate.ellis@fintechai.com> wrote:
> Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the acceptance targets are correct from our side. A few clarifications from NetOps: ...

Thanks Kate — a few technical notes and requests from Redwood infra: 

1) Peering/VPN specifics: if you do cross-account VPC peering we'll need the peer VPC ID, route table CIDRs, and the security group entries you want us to use. If VPN, please provide the VPN public IP, pre-shared-key (can be rotated), and allowed VPN subnet.

2) Ports and IPs: For the lab we'll need outbound TCP/443 to these action IPs: 34.82.19.101, 34.82.19.102, 34.82.19.103 (these are our test egress endpoints). If you have strict egress filtering, add those IPs for the 03/18 window.

3) Latency budget check: end-to-end includes your edge->peering->redwood worker->model inference->return. To meet p95 200ms we expect your edge-to-Redwood measured RTT (one-way) <= 40–60ms ideally. If your RTT is >80ms we will likely need to run an optimized batching/quantization plan or provision closer capacity.

4) Data capture: please include a pcap of a 5-minute synthetic run and a sample of your application-level logs (timestamps + request id) so we can correlate token timings with packet-level events.

Plan for Thursday: Rafael and Mina will run the Redwood side harness, capture kernel timestamps, and provide a timeline report. Priyom will coordinate scheduling/credentials.


--
Rafael Mendes
Infra Performance Lead | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

- Rafael (Redwood): prepare the harness and send a short pre-lab checklist by Mon 03/16 EOD.
